body:
Devon Price: anyone around to sanity check a weird precheck failure? seeing a false-positive on storage class detection in the private installer.

Devon Price: customer cluster (EKS) definitely has a default StorageClass but our precheck says:
```
[precheck] storage_class_default .......... FAILED
Reason: no default StorageClass detected
Remediation: ensure a StorageClass exists with annotation storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class=true
```
:thinking_face:

Ines Carvalho: do you have the raw debug output? sometimes kubectl is returning the beta annotation depending on cluster version.

Devon Price: yep, ran `redwood-private-installer upgrade precheck --debug` (sanitized):
```
DEBUG precheck.storageclass: running: kubectl get storageclass -o json
DEBUG precheck.storageclass: got 3 items
DEBUG precheck.storageclass: defaultCandidates=0
DEBUG precheck.storageclass: looked for annotation "storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class" == "true"
```

Devon Price: but `kubectl get sc` on the same cluster:
```
NAME            PROVISIONER             RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE      ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION   AGE
gp3 (default)   ebs.csi.aws.com         Delete          WaitForFirstConsumer   true                   221d
gp2             kubernetes.io/aws-ebs   Delete          WaitForFirstConsumer   true                   221d
efs-sc          efs.csi.aws.com         Delete          Immediate              true                   27d
```

Ethan Park: could be RBAC? but you’re getting items back, so probably not.

Ines Carvalho: can you dump the annotations from the JSON for gp3? just to confirm the key/value.

Devon Price: pulled it w/ jsonpath:
```
kubectl get sc gp3 -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations}'
map[storageclass.beta.kubernetes.io/is-default-class:true]
```

Devon Price: so it’s using the *beta* annotation key, not the stable one.

Sean Gallagher: :facepalm: we should definitely check both. we’ll hit this a lot on older clusters / long-lived EKS.

Connor O'Brien: +1. also worth handling case where it’s string "True" (capitalized) because I’ve seen that in the wild.

Devon Price: yeah, current check is basically:
- list storageclasses
- look for `storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class` == "true"
- fail if none

Devon Price: proposal:
1) accept either annotation key:
- `storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class`
- `storageclass.beta.kubernetes.io/is-default-class`
2) treat value case-insensitively ("true", "True", etc)
3) if multiple defaults (it happens), warn but pass

Ines Carvalho: + also, if neither annotation is present, we could fallback to detecting “(default)” in `kubectl get sc` output, but that’s gross. better keep it json-based.

Ethan Park: agree, json-based is fine. if we’re already parsing in Go, just check both keys.

Devon Price: here’s a quick patch sketch (Go) for the precheck:
```diff
- const defaultKey = "storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class"
+ var defaultKeys = []string{
+   "storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class",
+   "storageclass.beta.kubernetes.io/is-default-class",
+ }

  func isDefault(sc storagev1.StorageClass) bool {
    ann := sc.ObjectMeta.Annotations
-   return ann[defaultKey] == "true"
+   for _, k := range defaultKeys {
+     if v, ok := ann[k]; ok {
+       if strings.EqualFold(strings.TrimSpace(v), "true") {
+         return true
+       }
+     }
+   }
+   return false
  }
```

Devon Price: and if `defaultCount > 1`, surface as:
- severity: WARN
- message: “multiple default StorageClasses detected: [gp2 gp3]; installer will use chart value if set, otherwise cluster default resolution is undefined”

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: on WARN not FAIL. we shouldn’t hard stop upgrades for that.

Connor O'Brien: what’s the immediate workaround for the customer while we patch?

Devon Price: short term: either
- `--skip-precheck storage_class_default` (not ideal)
- or set explicit storage class in values (`global.storageClass=gp3`) so we don’t rely on default

Ines Carvalho: setting explicit is best. skipping precheck is scary if they actually *don’t* have a default.

Ethan Park: can you also update the remediation hint? right now it only mentions stable annotation key, which will mislead.

Devon Price: yep. will update remediation to:
“ensure at least one StorageClass exists and is marked default via annotation storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class=true (or storageclass.beta.kubernetes.io/is-default-class=true on older clusters)”

Sean Gallagher: can you drop a minimal repro in the test? just a fake SC object with beta annotation.

Devon Price: will do. I can add unit tests around `isDefault()` w/:
- stable key true
- beta key true
- stable key "True"
- no annotation -> false

Connor O'Brien: timeline? we’re trying to get this into the beta rehearsal this week.

Devon Price: I can have PR up today. it’s isolated to the precheck package.

Ines Carvalho: cool. please ping me on review.

Devon Price: will do. also adding a debug line to print which key matched (stable vs beta) so support can see it in diagnostics.

Sean Gallagher: +1. that’ll help with weird customer clusters.

Devon Price: posting customer-facing workaround text here in case Support asks:
“Your cluster marks default StorageClass using legacy annotation `storageclass.beta.kubernetes.io/is-default-class`. As a workaround, set `global.storageClass` to your desired class (e.g., `gp3`) or upgrade installer to version including the storage class precheck fix.”

Connor O'Brien: :white_check_mark: thanks. please link the PR here once it’s up.

Devon Price: PR going up shortly, will link in-thread.
